Tosafot on Bava Batra 43a:10:1.hebrew: ה"ג - ותסברא? עניים שקלי ודיינין מיפסלי? [אלא] ה"נ בספר תורה, ואמאי קרי להו עניים כו':
Tosafot on Bava Batra 43a:10:1.english: So we read [in the Gemara]: "And do you think that the poor take [the money], yet the judges are disqualified? Rather, here too [it is speaking] of a Torah scroll. And why does he call them 'poor'?" etc.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 43a:2:1.hebrew: אין לי עסק בה לא אמר כלום - וא"ת דבפרק השולח (גיטין דף מג: ושם), גבי מוכר עבדו לנכרי כו', אמר: היכי דמי אונו? דכתב ליה "לכשתברח ממנו אין לי עסק בך". אלמא "אין לי עסק בך" הוי לשון טוב! ואור"י, דאין לי עסק בך משמע "אלא תהא לעצמך", וגבי עבד דמהני "הרי את לעצמך", מהני נמי "אין לי עסק בך". אבל בשדה, דלא שייך למימר "הרי את לעצמך", כי אמר נמי "אין לי עסק בך" לא אמר כלום. דכיון דליכא לפרושי "אין לי עסק בך" אלא "תהא לעצמך" גבי שדה כמו גבי עבד, לא משמע גבי שדה "אין לי עסק בה" אלא סילוק דין ודברים, כדמוכח בכריתות (דף כד:):
Tosafot on Bava Batra 43a:2:1.english: "I have no dealings with it" – he has said nothing - And if you will ask: In the chapter Hashole'ach (Gittin 43b, there), regarding one who sells his slave to a gentile, etc., [the Gemara] said: What is the case of [the slave's] "ones" (a situation beyond his control)? Where [the seller] wrote to him, "When you flee from him, I have no dealings with you." Evidently, "I have no dealings with you" is a good (effective) expression! And Rabbi Yitzchak (the Ri) answered: "I have no dealings with you" implies "rather, you shall belong to yourself." And regarding a slave, where "you are your own [person]" is effective, "I have no dealings with you" is also effective. But regarding a field, where it is not applicable to say "you are your own," even when he says "I have no dealings with you," he has said nothing. For since it is not possible to explain "I have no dealings with you" as anything other than "you shall belong to yourself" in the case of a field, as it is in the case of a slave, [the phrase] "I have no dealings with it" regarding a field implies nothing other than a relinquishing of claims and disputes (i.e., of litigation), as is proven in Keritot (24b):

Tosafot on Bava Batra 43a:4:1.hebrew: מפני שמעמידה בפני בעל חובו - וא"ת, מאי איריא "מפני שמעמידה"? תיפוק ליה משום דלא ניחא ליה דתיהוי תרעומת עליו, כדאמרי' בפ"ק דב"ק (דף ח:): ראובן שמכר שדה לשמעון שלא באחריות, ואתא בעל חובו וקטריף לה מיניה — דינא הוא דאתי ראובן ומשתעי דינא בהדיה, ולא מצי א"ל לאו בעל דברים דידי את, דא"ל לא ניחא לי דתיהוי לשמעון תרעומת עילואי. וי"ל דאין נפסל בשביל כך לעדות. א"נ הכא מיירי אפילו במכיר בה שהיא שלו, דליכא תרעומת:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 43a:4:1.english: "Because he stands it [the field] before his creditor" - If you ask: Why does [the Gemara] specifically say "because he stands it"? Let it derive [the disqualification] instead from the fact that he is not pleased that there should be a grievance against him, as we say in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (8b): If Reuven sold a field to Shimon without a guarantee, and Reuven's creditor came and seized it from [Shimon] — it is right that Reuven should come and argue the case alongside him, and [the creditor] cannot say to him, "You are not my litigant," because [Reuven] can say, "It is not pleasing to me that Shimon should have a grievance against me." And one can answer that he is not disqualified from testifying because of this. Alternatively, here [the Gemara] speaks even of a case where he recognizes that it [the field] is his [the creditor's], so that there is no grievance.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 43a:6:1.hebrew: וליסלקו בי תרי מינייהו ולידיינו - וא"ת: והא בעינן "תחילתו וסופו בכשרות", והכא הוי תחילה בפסול, והוי כמו קרוב ונתרחק? ואור"י: דלא שייך "תחילתו בפסלות" הכא, כיון שאין פסלות תלוי בגוף אלא בממון:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 43a:6:1.english: "Let two of them withdraw, and let [the other two] judge" - And if you ask: But we require that "its beginning and its end be in a state of fitness," and here it was at the beginning in a state of disqualification, and it is like a relative who became distanced [from the litigant]? And Rabbi Yitzchak (the Ri) answers: That "its beginning in a state of disqualification" is not relevant here, since the disqualification is not dependent on the person's body [i.e., a personal status], but on money [i.e., a financial interest].
